capability: Evaluate the 16-term Faddeeva variant with its default order and declared failure contract.
discovery.boundary: Real axis is accepted; exponential continuation overflow raises.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for non-finite/empty phase points, a nonpositive or out-of-range integer order, or an unsupported pole count.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError when the continued fraction or pole sum exceeds float64 range; no silent clamp is applied.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Fixed-order approximation has no iterative convergence claim; truncation error is bounded only on the tested envelopes.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial value is returned after a failed call.

scope: Default and explicit order, scalar/matrix shapes, reflection, normalization, positive imaginary axis overflow regression.
80-digit mpmath equation grid and 70-digit independent Gaussian Cauchy integrals.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to the declared relation: Weideman rational FFT expansion with erfcx on imaginary axis. Evidence: test_generalized_dispersion_faddeeva_variants.py, test_generalized_dispersion_faddeeva_independent.py (9 recorded test functions; shared-file coverage only; independent analytic/high-precision oracle); the contract example ran. Excluded scope: A guaranteed global error bound; An arbitrary distribution response.
known_limitations: Fixed truncation error depends on phase point and order.
Only shared-file coverage is bound (test_generalized_dispersion_faddeeva_variants.py); no asset-specific failure/limit probe is recorded.

summary: Evaluate the 16-term Faddeeva variant with its default order and declared failure contract.

identity.definition: Weideman rational FFT expansion with erfcx on imaginary axis.
identity.boundary: Real axis is accepted; exponential continuation overflow raises.

supported: Finite nonempty scalar or array input; shape preserved.
preconditions: All phase values and computed results fit complex128.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Rational truncation or pole count. None selects order 16.
inputs.constraints: Any positive integer order. Boolean rejected.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_faddeeva_dr
import numpy as np
r=evaluate_faddeeva_dr(0.2+0.7j)
assert np.isfinite(r["w"])
example.expected: Observed PASS: Finite complex response at the effective order.

references: Weideman (1994), Computation of the Complex Error Function, doi:10.1137/0731077
Xie (2013), Generalized Plasma Dispersion Function, arXiv:1305.6476
